extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short science fiction and fantasy to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting original short science fiction and fantasy stories to Clarkesworld Magazine, including acceptable genres, length, formatting, rights, payment, and submission/process rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should aim for the preferred length (4000) but may submit works between 1000 and 8000 words. Very short or very long pieces outside that window are not within the stated guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate
rubrics_metrics.description: 10¢ per word up to 4000 words, 5¢ per word after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment policy applies per word; clarifies compensation tiers. No additional scoring guidance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction and fantasy (includes horror and related subgenres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science fiction need not be strictly 'hard' SF; fantasy can be folkloric, medieval, contemporary, surreal, etc. Horror may be supernatural or psychological, as long as it is frightening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions and correspondence should be in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazine claims first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights (author must be willing to sign 100+ chapbooks), and non-exclusive anthology rights for the Realms yearly anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect to grant these rights if accepted; the magazine will also include accepted fiction in chapbooks and annual collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be well-written; 'language is important.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors state there is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing.' Strong prose and use of language are essential to a successful story.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid very long paragraphs or typographical trickery, which may work against you for an online magazine format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science fiction rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plausibility, internal consistency, and thoughtful handling of speculative elements are valued even when the story is not strictly 'hard' science fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of profanity, gore, and sexuality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no absolute barriers to profanity, gore, or sexuality; however, high amounts are generally used poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include heavy profanity, gore, or sexual content, ensure it is used skillfully and serves the story rather than being gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely hard sells / things to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of story types and tropes that are unlikely to be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is the sole obstacle to catching a criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory; stories using the words 'thou' or 'thine'; talking cats; talking swords; stories where the climax depends on the spilling of intestines; stories where FTL travel is as easy as on television or movies; time travel (marked as a hard sell); stories that depend on vestigial belief in Judeo-Christian mythology to be frightening (examples given); stories about rapist-murderer-cannibals; stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING (a body, an alien craft, Excalibur, ANYTHING); stories about material recently covered in Scientific American (three months ago); stories where contemporary political parties take over the world and either save or ruin it; AD&D game transcripts or essentially-game-play stories; 'funny' stories that depend on or include puns; 'sexy vampires,' wanton werewolves, or lusty pirates; zombies or 'zombie-wannabes'; stories originally intended for someone's upcoming theme anthology or issue; stories where the protagonist is widely despised or admired simply because he/she is so smart and/or strange; stories depicting an 'artsy-fartsy bohemia' as written by an author who clearly has not experienced one; and 'trunk stories' (previously written and shelved material). These are described as 'likely hard sells' rather than absolute prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method & allowed file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions accepted only via the online submissions system; no email or paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online submissions form (links provided). Stories should be in standard manuscript format and may be submitted as .RTF or .DOC files. The submission form requests name, email, cover letter, story title, and story file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter should contain the length of your story, your publishing history, and any other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant, concise information (example given: if you send a lusty pirate story and happen to BE a lusty pirate, mention that). Keep cover letters professional and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submission and resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous submissions; do not resubmit rejected stories or query for permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submitting, a tracking number appears and an automated confirmation email is sent—contact the editor if not received within 24 hours. Average response time is under two days but may be up to a week. Do not send queries until after a two-week period; check blog/forum for announcements first. Do not send revisions unless specifically requested. Do not submit another story for seven days after receiving a rejection. Do not re-submit rejected stories or argue with rejection slips. Writers whose work is accepted may not submit again until six months after their story is published. If uncertain about any policy, follow the most conservative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking & contact procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A tracking number is displayed after submission and used to monitor status; automated confirmation email will be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confirmation email is not received within 24 hours, email the editor. Note: some email providers (e.g., Yahoo) may treat automated mail as spam—check spam folders.
